explanation.text:
(Pro. 28:1-28)

A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold (Pro 14:26; Psa 27:1).

bsb.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.

explanation.text:
Anarchy producing contending rulers shortens the reign of each.

but by a man . . . prolonged--or, "by a man of understanding--that is, a good ruler--he who knows or regards the right, that is, a good citizen, shall prolong (his days)." Good rulers are a blessing to the people. Bad government as a punishment for evil is contrasted with good as blessing to the good.

bsb.text: A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.

explanation.text: A poor man, etc.--Such, in power, exact more severely, and so leave subjects bare.

bsb.text: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.

explanation.text: They that forsake . . . wicked--Wrongdoers encourage one another.

bsb.text: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.

explanation.text: (Compare Joh 7:17). Ignorance of moral truth is due to unwillingness to know it.

bsb.text: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 10:6). Riches cannot compensate for sin, nor the want of them affect integrity.

bsb.text: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 17:25).

riotous men--or, "gluttons" (Pro 23:20-21).

bsb.text: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.

explanation.text: usury . . . unjust gain--(Compare Margin). The two terms, meaning nearly the same, may denote excessive interest. God's providence directs the proper use of wealth.

bsb.text: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 15:8; Pro 21:27).

hearing--that is, obeying. God requires sincere worshippers (Psa 66:18; Joh 4:24).

bsb.text: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 26:27).

bsb.text: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.

explanation.text: A poor but wise man can discover (and expose) the rich and self-conceited.

bsb.text: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.

explanation.text:
great glory--or, cause for it to a people, for the righteous rejoice in good, and righteousness exalts a nation (Pro 14:34).

a man . . . hidden--that is, the good retire, or all kinds try to escape a wicked rule.

bsb.text: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 32:3-5). Concealment of sin delivers none from God's wrath, but He shows mercy to the humble penitent (Psa 51:4).

bsb.text: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.

explanation.text:
feareth--that is, God, and so repents.

hardeneth his heart--makes himself insensible to sin, and so will not repent (Pro 14:16; Pro 29:1).

bsb.text: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.

explanation.text: The rapacity and cruelty of such beasts well represent some wicked men (compare Psa 7:2; Psa 17:12).

bsb.text: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

explanation.text: The prince . . . understanding--that is, He does not perceive that oppression jeopards his success. Covetousness often produces oppression, hence the contrast.

bsb.text: A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.

explanation.text:
doeth violence . . . blood, etc.--or, that is oppressed by the blood of life (Gen 9:6), which he has taken.

to the pit--the grave or destruction (Pro 1:12; Job 33:18-24; Psa 143:7).

stay him--sustain or deliver him.

bsb.text: A man burdened by bloodguilt will flee into the Pit; let no one support him.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 10:9; Pro 17:20). Double dealing is eventually fatal.

bsb.text: He who walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:4; Pro 20:4).

vain persons--idle, useless drones, implying that they are also wicked (Pro 12:11; Psa 26:4).

bsb.text: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.

explanation.text: maketh haste . . . rich--implying deceit or fraud (Pro 20:21), and so opposed to "faithful" or reliable.

bsb.text: A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.

explanation.text: respect of persons-- (Pro 24:23). Such are led to evil by the slightest motive.

bsb.text: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 28:20).

evil eye--in the general sense of Pro 23:6, here more specific for covetousness (compare Pro 22:9; Mat 20:15).

poverty . . . him--by God's providence.

bsb.text: A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 9:8-9; Pro 27:5). Those benefited by reproof will love their monitors.

bsb.text: He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.

explanation.text: (Compare Mat 15:4-6). Such, though heirs, are virtually thieves, to be ranked with highwaymen.

bsb.text: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.

explanation.text:
of a proud heart--literally, "puffed up of soul"--that is, self-confident, and hence overbearing and litigious.

made fat--or, "prosperous" (Pro 11:25; Pro 16:20).

bsb.text: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 3:6-8).

walketh wisely--that is, trusting in God (Pro 22:17-19).

bsb.text: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:24-26).

hideth his eyes--as the face (Psa 27:9; Psa 69:17), denotes inattention.

bsb.text: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.

explanation.text:
The elevation of the wicked to power drives men to seek refuge from tyranny (compare Pro 28:12; Pro 11:10; Psa 12:8).

Next: Proverbs Chapter 29

bsb.text: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
